Standard: 1.P.EICC.4.c
Domain primary: Writing
Domain secondary: Speaking & Listening, Comprehension
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Generate ideas for writing by using what they already know, gathering information from texts, and talking with others.
Skills:
- Generate ideas for writing by assessing prior knowledge.
- Generate ideas for writing by gathering information from texts.
- Generate ideas for writing by engaging in discussions with others.
Observable behaviors:
- Recall and use prior knowledge to think of writing topics.
- Find information in texts to help develop writing ideas.
- Participate in discussions to share and develop ideas for writing.
Pedagogy terms: generate ideas, prior knowledge, gather information, discussions, writing process
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify prior knowledge relevant to a writing topic.
- oral_production: Participate in discussions to share ideas for writing.
- procedural_application: Use prior knowledge and information from texts to generate ideas for writing.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how prior knowledge, information from texts, and discussions help generate writing ideas.
- comprehension_response: Gather information from texts to support writing ideas.
Codes: 1.P.EICC.4.c

Standard: 1.P.ST.2.c
Domain primary: Writing
Domain secondary: Comprehension, Language
Cognitive demand: DOK3_strategic_thinking
Competency: Use understanding of how authors think about context and audience to choose important information, accessible text design, effective words and language, and impactful craft techniques when creating or interpreting texts.
Skills:
- Draw from knowledge of how authors consider context and audience to determine which information and ideas to highlight.
- Determine which text design is most accessible for the intended audience.
- Decide which word choices and language structures are most effective for the audience and purpose.
- Identify which craft techniques are most impactful in the text.
Observable behaviors:
- Identify which information and ideas an author highlights based on context and audience.
- Recognize text designs that make information easier to understand for the intended audience.
- Notice word choices and language structures that suit the audience and purpose.
- Observe craft techniques authors use to make their texts more effective.
Pedagogy terms: author's purpose, audience, context, text design, word choice, language structures, craft techniques
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Recognize how authors select information and design texts for their audience and context.
- procedural_application: Apply knowledge of audience and context to determine effective information, text design, word choice, language, and craft techniques.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how authors consider context and audience to make choices about information, text design, language, and craft techniques.
- comprehension_response: Respond to texts by identifying how author choices reflect audience and context considerations.
Codes: 1.P.ST.2.c

Standard: 1.P.EICC.4
Domain primary: Writing
Domain secondary: Language
Cognitive demand: DOK3_strategic_thinking
Competency: Compose various texts for different purposes and audiences by planning, drafting, evaluating, revising, and editing your writing.
Skills:
- Establish a purpose and goals for writing and identify a target audience.
- Plan how to organize the text by selecting modes, genres, and structures that will achieve the purpose and meet the needs of the target audience.
- Generate ideas for content by assessing prior knowledge, gathering information from texts, and engaging in discussions with others.
- Link ideas and information to the organization plan, highlighting ideas and information that are most relevant, useful, and impactful.
- Construct an initial draft by integrating ideas and information; selecting words, phrases, and sentences; and incorporating craft techniques that will best achieve the purpose of the text and resonate with the target audience.
- Evaluate the text's effectiveness based on self-review or feedback from others, determining whether the text matches the purpose and goals for writing.
- Make changes to the text based on self-evaluation or external feedback, revising the organization, ideas, information, word choices, and craft techniques in order to increase the text's effectiveness.
- Edit the text, ensuring it adheres to the conventions of written language.
Observable behaviors:
- Set a clear purpose and goals for writing and identify who will read the text.
- Plan how to organize writing by choosing modes, genres, and structures that fit the purpose and audience.
- Generate ideas by using what you know, reading texts, and talking with others.
- Connect ideas and information to your plan, focusing on the most important and useful points.
- Create a first draft by combining ideas and choosing words and sentences that fit the purpose and audience.
- Review your writing or get feedback to see if it meets your goals and purpose.
- Make changes to improve organization, ideas, word choice, and writing techniques based on review or feedback.
- Edit your writing to follow correct language rules and conventions.
Pedagogy terms: writing process, purpose, audience, planning, drafting, revising, editing, feedback, organization, word choice
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify the purpose and audience for writing.
- written_production: Write drafts and final texts for different purposes and audiences.
- matching_sorting_sequencing: Organize ideas and information to fit the writing plan.
- procedural_application: Apply writing processes including planning, drafting, revising, and editing.
- investigation_handson: Gather information from texts and discussions to generate ideas.
- reasoning_explanation: Evaluate the effectiveness of writing based on goals and feedback.
- comprehension_response: Respond to feedback and revise writing to improve clarity and impact.
Codes: 1.P.EICC.4
candidates.label: Writing Processes

candidates.text:
Standard: 1.P.AC.3
Domain primary: Writing
Domain secondary: Comprehension, Speaking & Listening
Cognitive demand: DOK3_strategic_thinking
Competency: Understand and use how text design affects audience and purpose when reading and creating texts in different modes and genres.
Skills:
- Explore and create texts in various modes and genres, developing and applying knowledge of how specific features impact meaning, tone, style, purpose, and audience.
- Apply knowledge of how mode and genre impact what kinds of ideas and information are included in texts.
- Apply knowledge of how mode and genre impact how ideas and information are structured and arranged in texts.
- Consume and produce multimodal texts, integrating a variety of genres, text features, and craft techniques to influence target audiences and achieve specific purposes.
Observable behaviors:
- Identify how features of different text modes and genres affect meaning, tone, style, purpose, and audience.
- Create texts in various modes and genres using features that influence meaning and audience.
- Explain how the mode and genre determine the kinds of ideas and information included in a text.
- Explain how the mode and genre affect the structure and arrangement of ideas and information in a text.
- Read and create multimodal texts that combine genres, text features, and craft techniques to influence audiences and achieve purposes.
Pedagogy terms: text design, mode, genre, text features, audience, purpose, multimodal texts, author's craft
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify how text features in different modes and genres affect meaning and audience.
- written_production: Create texts in various modes and genres using features that influence meaning and audience.
- procedural_application: Apply knowledge of how mode and genre impact the ideas, information, structure, and arrangement in texts.
- investigation_handson: Explore and create texts in various modes and genres to understand how features impact meaning, tone, style, purpose, and audience.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how mode and genre affect the content and structure of texts and how text design influences audience and purpose.
- comprehension_response: Consume multimodal texts integrating genres, text features, and craft techniques to understand their influence on audience and purpose.
Codes: 1.P.AC.3
candidates.label: Text Design

candidates.text:
Standard: 1.T.T.1.e
Domain primary: Writing
Domain secondary: Comprehension
Cognitive demand: DOK3_strategic_thinking
Competency: Use knowledge of narrative techniques such as characters, settings, and events to create texts that share real or imagined experiences and include a sense of closure.
Skills:
- Use knowledge of characters in narratives to create texts.
- Use knowledge of settings in narratives to create texts.
- Use knowledge of events in narratives to create texts.
- Create texts that share real or imagined experiences and events.
- Include a sense of closure in created texts.
Observable behaviors:
- Create stories that include characters, settings, and events.
- Write narratives that describe real or imagined experiences.
- Include a clear ending that provides closure to the story.
Pedagogy terms: narrative techniques, characters, settings, events, sense of closure, narrative writing
Required student actions:
- written_production: Write texts that use characters, settings, and events to tell a story with a clear ending.
- procedural_application: Apply knowledge of narrative techniques to create coherent stories.
Codes: 1.T.T.1.e

Standard: 1.T.SS.2
Domain primary: Writing
Domain secondary: Language
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Students identify descriptive words in texts and use descriptive words to create engaging writing.
Skills:
- Identify descriptive words in texts.
- Explain the use of descriptive words in texts.
- Use descriptive words to craft engaging texts.
Observable behaviors:
- Point out descriptive words in a story or text.
- Explain why certain words make the text more interesting.
- Use descriptive words when writing sentences or short texts.
- Choose words that help readers picture what is being described.
Pedagogy terms: descriptive words, engaging language, word choice, writing
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify descriptive words in texts.
- written_production: Use descriptive words to write engaging texts.
- procedural_application: Use descriptive words to craft engaging texts.
- representation_modeling: Explain the use of descriptive words in texts.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain why descriptive words are used in texts.
Codes: 1.T.SS.2
candidates.label: Craft

candidates.text:
Standard: 1.P.EICC.2.a
Domain primary: Writing
Domain secondary: Speaking & Listening
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Tell or share real or imagined experiences by creating or interpreting stories in spoken or written form.
Skills:
- Share real experiences by telling or writing stories.
- Share imagined experiences by telling or writing stories.
- Interpret stories that tell or include real or imagined experiences.
Observable behaviors:
- Tell a story about something that really happened or something made up.
- Create a story by drawing or writing.
- Listen to or read a story and explain what happened.
- Share stories with others through speaking or writing.
Pedagogy terms: storytelling, narrative, experience sharing, interpretation, composition
Required student actions:
- oral_production: Tell or share stories about real or imagined experiences orally.
- written_production: Write or draw stories that tell about real or imagined experiences.
- comprehension_response: Interpret stories to understand real or imagined experiences.
Codes: 1.P.EICC.2.a

Standard: 1.P.EICC.2
Domain primary: Speaking & Listening
Domain secondary: Writing, Comprehension
Cognitive demand: DOK3_strategic_thinking
Competency: Engage in written or spoken conversations as both a speaker and listener for different tasks and purposes, making meaningful connections within and across texts and to real life.
Skills:
- Engage in spoken or written dialogue as an author and audience.
- Make intentional connections within texts.
- Make intentional connections between texts.
- Make intentional connections beyond texts to other knowledge or experiences.
Observable behaviors:
- Participate in dialogues by sharing ideas and responding to others.
- Make connections between different texts during discussions.
- Relate ideas from texts to personal experiences or other knowledge.
- Use spoken or written language intentionally to communicate for various purposes.
Pedagogy terms: dialogue, author and audience, text connections, purposeful communication
Required student actions:
- oral_production: Speak and respond in dialogues for different purposes.
- written_production: Write to communicate ideas and respond to texts.
- procedural_application: Use dialogue skills to connect ideas within and between texts.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain connections made between texts and ideas during dialogue.
- comprehension_response: Respond thoughtfully to texts and peers in spoken or written form.
Codes: 1.P.EICC.2
candidates.label: Engagement & Intention

candidates.text:
Standard: 1.P.EICC.1.e
Domain primary: Speaking & Listening
Domain secondary: Writing, Comprehension
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Participate actively in a community of readers and writers by following group norms, discussing texts, sharing writing, listening to others, and giving and receiving feedback.
Skills:
- Develop group norms for participation in a community of readers and writers
- Discuss texts with others in the group
- Share individual writing with the group
- Listen to others as they share their writing
- Offer feedback on peers' writing
- Respond to feedback received on own writing
Observable behaviors:
- Follow agreed-upon group norms during reading and writing activities
- Discuss texts with peers by sharing ideas and listening to others
- Share individual writing pieces with the group
- Listen attentively as others share their writing
- Offer constructive feedback on peers' writing
- Respond appropriately to feedback received on own writing
Pedagogy terms: community of readers and writers, group norms, discussion, sharing writing, listening, feedback
Required student actions:
- oral_production: Discuss texts with peers and share writing aloud
- procedural_application: Follow group norms during reading and writing activities
- reasoning_explanation: Offer and respond to feedback on writing
- comprehension_response: Listen attentively to others' writing and participate in text discussions
Codes: 1.P.EICC.1.e

Standard: 1.T.T.2.d
Domain primary: Writing
Domain secondary: Comprehension
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Use expository writing techniques to introduce a topic, provide facts about the topic, and give a sense of closure in writing.
Skills:
- Use knowledge of expository techniques to introduce a topic.
- Use knowledge of expository techniques to supply facts about the topic.
- Use knowledge of expository techniques to provide a sense of closure.
Observable behaviors:
- Write an introduction that states the topic clearly.
- Include facts that explain or describe the topic.
- Write a concluding sentence or statement that wraps up the information.
- Organize writing to show a clear beginning, middle, and end related to the topic.
Pedagogy terms: expository writing, introduction, facts, closure, topic, conclusion
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Recognize expository writing features such as introductions, facts, and conclusions in texts.
- written_production: Write an introduction, supply facts, and provide a closing statement about a topic.
- matching_sorting_sequencing: Sequence sentences or ideas to form a coherent expository paragraph with introduction, facts, and closure.
- procedural_application: Apply knowledge of expository techniques to organize writing about a topic.
- representation_modeling: Model writing that introduces a topic, includes facts, and ends with closure.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how the introduction, facts, and closure help shape understanding of the topic.
- comprehension_response: Respond to questions about the purpose of introductions, facts, and closure in expository texts.
Codes: 1.T.T.2.d
